workLog.activity: Bumped the pip-audit pin from 26.1.2 to 26.2 and moved its rationale comments with it
workLog.finding: The pin had already moved once for the same reason: issue #2438 set it to 26.1.2 to escape PYSEC-2026-196, and 26.1.2 has since become the vulnerable version under PYSEC-2026-3721. Three comment lines restated 26.1.2 next to the pin that owns it, so a bump that touched only line 505 would have left prose describing a version the workflow no longer installs. That is the same duplicated-value drift that broke tests/ci/test_validate_vendor_provenance.py on the setup-uv bump. Every mention moved together, and the comment now tells the next reader to expect a third move.

workLog.activity: Kept all three --ignore-vuln flags across the bump
workLog.finding: A clean virtualenv on pip 26.2 audits clean, which reads as license to drop the ignores. It is not. That venv resolved Pygments 2.21.0 while this project pins 2.19.2, which is what CVE-2026-4539 is about, so the result answers for a dependency set CI does not have. Dropping the ignores on that evidence would have turned this check red again on pygments. Retiring them is issue #1778's job, measured against the real tree.

workLog.activity: Established the failure is red on main, not on any one branch
workLog.finding: Main run 32486211457 at commit 63bca8796 lists Python Security Checks among its failed jobs. The newest main run reports success and looks like a refutation, but the job's conclusion there is skipped: the commit was documentation only and the path filter short-circuited it. A green run in which the job never executed is not evidence the job passes, and reading it as such would have closed this investigation with the wrong answer.
